stories.read: Big if real, years from done
stories.headline: Tesla, SpaceX form committees to study a merger
stories.move: On SpaceX's Oct. 20 Q3 earnings call, its first since going public, Musk said Tesla's and SpaceX's boards have each formed a special committee of independent directors, at shareholders' request, to study a possible combination of the two companies. Musk said he is a conflicted party and cannot take part in the committees' discussions. He said no deal terms exist yet and flagged that a Tesla shareholder vote would need support from 50% of all outstanding shares, not just those cast, calling that a high bar. SpaceX reported Q3 revenue of $14.6 billion, up 161% year over year and above the $12.72 billion analysts expected; shares rose about 10% in premarket trading the next day.
stories.why: A combined company would be one of the largest corporate mergers ever, and investors have speculated about it for months given growing operational overlap between the two firms.
stories.bear: The special committees could study the idea for a long time without reaching an agreement, and Musk said the shareholder-approval bar on the Tesla side is unusually high.
stories.watch: Whether Tesla's board raises a merger proposal at its annual meeting.

stories.read: Embarrassing outage, not a financial hit
stories.headline: Google Cloud outage knocks out UK banking apps
stories.move: A Google Cloud outage in its London region (europe-west2) on Oct. 20 disrupted banking apps and other services across the UK and Europe for several hours. Google attributed the disruption to a power event in one zone. Lloyds, Halifax, HSBC and Revolut customers reported being unable to log in or access funds, and court video hearings and delivery services including Royal Mail and DPD were also affected. Google said the issue was mitigated for most customers by the next day, though a small number remained affected.
stories.why: The outage shows how concentrated some of the UK's banking infrastructure is on a single cloud provider and zone.
stories.bear: Google said the root cause was a physical power failure, not a security breach, and most customers recovered within hours.
stories.watch: Whether Google publishes a post-incident report naming additional affected customers.

stories.headline: Nvidia's Huang defends CoreWeave after debt worries hit stock
stories.move: Speaking in Stockholm on Oct. 15, Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang said "CoreWeave's strength is improving every day" and that its cost of capital is falling, adding he sees no need for Nvidia to backstop the company. The comments came a day after CoreWeave shares fell 15% to $65.78, their biggest one-day drop since February, as investors grew worried about the AI cloud company's debt load. CoreWeave shares recovered after Huang's remarks, closing up 5.9% at $69.69.
stories.why: Nvidia is both an investor in and major supplier to CoreWeave, so Huang's confidence carries weight for a company whose borrowing has drawn scrutiny.
stories.bear: Huang's comments are a view, not a financing commitment, and CoreWeave's debt load and the cost of insuring it against default remain elevated.
stories.watch: CoreWeave's next quarterly results and any update on its borrowing costs.

stories.read: India's biggest IPO, by a wide margin
stories.headline: Reliance's Jio Platforms opens India's largest-ever IPO
stories.move: Jio Platforms opened its initial public offering to the public on Oct. 21, with a price band of 1,065 to 1,119 rupees per share. At the top of that band the fresh-issue offering would raise about 30,213 crore rupees (roughly $3.6 billion), which Indian financial press describe as the country's largest-ever IPO by issue size. Subscription closes Oct. 23. Reliance Industries holds more than 66% of Jio Platforms, with a Meta affiliate near 10% and Google holding about 7.7%, according to LSEG data.
stories.why: A successful listing would give Ambani's Reliance a large new source of capital and a public market valuation for its telecom and digital arm.
stories.bear: The final issue price and allotment results won't be known until subscription closes, and Reliance retains firm control regardless of how the public portion prices.
stories.watch: Jio Platforms' subscription numbers when the window closes Oct. 23, and its stock-market debut.

stories.read: Overhang removed, not a new contract
stories.headline: Palantir settles London lawsuit over scrapped police deal
stories.move: Palantir and the Mayor of London's Office for Policing and Crime (Mopac) settled, on Oct. 14, the lawsuit Palantir had brought after Mopac blocked a roughly £50 million deal for the Metropolitan Police to use Palantir's AI-driven crime-analysis software. Both sides withdrew their allegations against each other. Palantir had argued the block was an unlawful veto based on the firm's "values and ethics"; Mopac said its decision rested on procurement process, not on Palantir specifically. The Met has opened a fresh competition for the analytics contract.
stories.why: The settlement clears Palantir to compete again for a UK police contract it had been shut out of, at a time when the firm is also facing a separate review of an NHS contract in Britain.
stories.bear: Palantir isn't guaranteed to win the re-opened competition, and UK scrutiny of its government contracts continues on other fronts.
stories.watch: The outcome of the Met's new procurement competition for the analytics contract.

stories.headline: Eric Schmidt's early Anthropic bet nears a payday
stories.move: Bloomberg reported Oct. 19 that former Google CEO Eric Schmidt holds about a 1% stake in Anthropic, stemming from an early investment in the AI company's 2021 Series A round. Anthropic filed confidentially for an IPO on June 1 after a $65 billion funding round valued it at $965 billion, and some investors have discussed a listing valuation of around $1.5 trillion, with a listing possible as early as this fall. It is unclear whether Schmidt has sold any of his stake; he and Anthropic did not respond to requests for comment.
stories.why: A roughly 1% stake at that scale of valuation would make Schmidt one of the largest individual beneficiaries of an Anthropic listing.
stories.bear: Anthropic has not confirmed an IPO date or valuation, and reported target valuations for the listing have varied widely across reports.
stories.watch: Whether Anthropic sets a formal IPO date and price range this fall.

stories.read: Debt markets pricing in AI concentration risk
stories.headline: SoftBank's credit risk hits its highest since 2022
stories.move: SoftBank Group's five-year credit-default-swap spread climbed to about 432 basis points on Oct. 20, a level unseen since late 2022, according to Bloomberg, as investors weigh the company's heavy financial commitments to OpenAI against reports it is in early talks to acquire security firm Allied Universal for about $18 billion. SoftBank has already raised a $40 billion bridge loan and a separate $10 billion loan collateralized by its OpenAI stake to fund its AI investments, and its OpenAI stake is on track to reach roughly $64.6 billion by October.
stories.why: Rising default-insurance costs signal that credit investors see SoftBank's AI bets, and the debt funding them, as increasingly concentrated risk.
stories.bear: SoftBank's stock has still risen sharply this year on optimism about its OpenAI stake, even as its credit spreads widen.
stories.watch: Whether SoftBank confirms or drops the reported Allied Universal acquisition talks.

watch: Jio Platforms IPO subscription window closes Oct. 23, with a stock-market debut to follow.
Tesla reports its own Q3 2026 earnings after the close on Oct. 21.
Whether Tesla's and SpaceX's special merger committees reach an agreement before Tesla's annual meeting.
memo: Two of the year's biggest AI spenders, Oracle and SoftBank, just saw the cost of insuring their own debt hit multi-year records — credit markets are pricing AI buildout risk that stock markets haven't yet.
A single cloud provider's outage knocked UK banking apps offline for hours — know which of your own vendors or cloud zones would take you down if they failed.
Palantir's London settlement shows a blocked public contract isn't necessarily dead — it can come back to life months later if you keep pressing a procurement challenge rather than walking away.

movers.why: Amazon climbed 5.0% after Morgan Stanley named it a top pick and raised its price target, citing AWS's AI growth.
